reason: Connecting the circulation to the filter seems necessary to give filtered fluid a separate route, and it is the only offered action.
expectation: I expect blood to reach the filter and some fluid to enter the receiving tubule; I am unsure how much detail the result will give.

effect: The filter lets glucose enter the filtrate along with water, salts and urea, so the next goal is to recover it.
reaction: The distinction between filtrate and finished urine is useful, and the glucose makes the recovery step meaningful.
reason: The proximal recovery lining is the only offered combination and seems suited to returning glucose from the filtrate.
expectation: I expect the lining to recover glucose from the tubule, probably returning it to the blood, though I am unsure how the result will explain it.

effect: The lining returns glucose, salts and much of the filtered water to the blood, while fluid containing waste continues through the tubule. That completes the chapter's goals.
reaction: The broad recovery of useful substances makes the filter-and-recovery sequence clearer, though I would have liked more explanation of how the lining moves them.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting circulation to the filter was most worthwhile because the result distinguished filtrate from finished urine and showed why useful glucose needs to be recovered.

leastWorthwhile.text: The recovery step was predictable because it was the only combination offered and the goal effectively named its purpose. Its result also left the mechanism of recovery unexplained.

surprise.text: The filter letting useful glucose leave the blood helped me understand why filtration must be followed by recovery.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt purposeless: both followed directly from the stated goals. The choices were prescribed, though, so I did not have to work out compatibility.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in another chapter if it offered more meaningful choices or explained the mechanisms in greater depth; this chapter was clear but very brief and directed.
